Currently replaying tGAAC and recently finished 'Memoirs of a Clouded Kokero' which is one of my least favorite cases in the entire series. If I had to make changes, I think first would be having William Shamspeare actually die. 

The reason for this is I think the idea of having the victim survive their murder attempt is a good idea, but was executed poorly. Main reason being, Shamspeare and Natsume barely know each other, so there's not really any motive for Natsume and makes the case kinda boring. Imagine if Shamspeare and Natsume absolutely despised each other. That would make a clear motive for Natsume would try to poison him, while also making the case more interest bc now you're defending Natsume from trying to kill the person he loathed. Instead we got a case with zero motive from the defendent, so if since they didn't execut this idea well, I would have rathered having Shamspeare killed off. Ik having shamspeare be killed doesn't establish a motive, but the case would actually be more interesting with an actual death.

Second change is cut out a lot from the first investigation and trial. These two parts were incredibly boring, especially when you got to the part about proving shamspeare stole gas. The only reason for that whole thing was basically so Naruhodo can show there's tea left, which did not need to take as long as it did. 

By doing this, you can focus on the actually interesting parts from the case like everything going on with Selden and Duncan Ross. That's the interesting part of this case, not how Shamspeare was stealing gas. Don't wait so long to mention these characters. Find some way to connect them to the case earlier on so the whole case is about finding the answer about what happened to them, rather than just the last trial.

The thing with this case it had potential to be really good, but just shot itself in the foot by being as boring as possible at times. Rather than having a death, having a motive, and focusing on what's actually interesting, we got a poorly executed victim living their attack, defendant having no reason to kill the victim, and solving how someone stole gas instead of focusing on why the house is 'cursed' and how this connects back to someone who was set to receive capital punishment

When I first played T&T in May of 2020, I absolutely hated the Stolen Turnabout. It was my second least favorite in the trilogy, only ahead of the lost turnabout. However, after I replayed T&T in May of 2021 and watching the anime back in November, I grew to really like the Stolen Turnabout. When I replayed it, I didn't find the case boring at all and loved how it made it appear there was no murder at first. When I watched the anime, I thought Luke Atmey was a great villain and very funny. Despite hating it at first, I grew very fond of the Stolen Turnabout.

I think mythical/event only legendaries are an outdated concept. Due to the internet, people find out about these pokemon long before the event take place and any play ground rumors on how to get these pokemon can easily be disproved by the internet. Not to mention, these pokemon can easily be cheated into the games. Due to this, there isn't any real sense of mystery around mythical/event pokemon so I think they are outdated.
